title: Node pool, 1-node emulations, profiling and integration branch
shape: D3-32 DP-rank slice (1 node, DCP4, EP4 emulating EP32) r8/r16/r24 at L132K; P3-16 DEP4-on-1-node slice (EP4 emulating EP16) F16K/F8K at L78K; 24-layer view
gap_analysis: Slices ready, first baselines queued. Key harness finding: the specialized decode fuses the MoE router GEMM into its front (reads moe.gate.weight + e_score_correction_bias directly), so the bench's --routing balanced fixture never reached the sdec graph; with dummy router weights each GPU of a 4-GPU slice touched all 224 local experts, 8x the deployed EP32 expert weight traffic (a 24-layer r8 slice measured 12.2 ms vs a 9.9 ms model achievable for the full 93-layer step). Fixed in the bench (no production change) by an expert-count emulation that restricts routing to 28 experts / GPU (decode) or 56 (prefill) at the deployed token-expert pairs per GPU.
inefficiencies: Slice deviation: 24-layer view (896 experts x 93 layers do not fit at EP4); model rows rescaled to the same layer counts
Slice deviation: MegaMoE dispatch/combine over 4 GPUs instead of 32 (decode) / 16 (prefill)
Slice deviation: DSpark preview drafter (24-layer target ids)
